note: Behaviour evals for the recipe. Run them in a throwaway fixture (git-local vcs_host, temp ledger, fake brain); never against a real board.

evals.name: hand-run-tick-reads-dispositions-first
evals.prompt: run the PR review loop by hand once — no scheduler, just do one tick. dry-run.
evals.expected_output: Takes the tick lock, then runs `pr_feed.py dispositions` (without --emit, since metrics were not asked for) before `unreviewed`, puts the one-line dispositions summary in the tick report, and lets nothing in it change which PRs are reviewed. Posting stays dry-run. Releases the lock and tears down worktrees in a finally. Does not claim that waved-off findings are suppressed next time.
assertions: Runs dispositions before unreviewed
Does NOT pass --emit to dispositions unasked
The report carries a dispositions line
Does NOT post live and does not mark --mode live
Does not claim a false-positive suppression store or automatic suppression exists
Releases the tick lock

evals.name: round-capped-pr-named-not-reviewed
evals.prompt: run one PR review tick by hand, dry-run. I think feature/export is the one that keeps bouncing back.
evals.expected_output: Takes the tick lock, runs dispositions, rounds and step-back --due (all without --live/--emit), then unreviewed. feature/export is under round_capped: it is not checked out, reviewed or marked, and the report has a Round-capped line naming it with its round count and that the step-back was only previewed. Any re-reviewed PR is judged on interdiff_command. The Spend line is unchanged. Releases the lock in a finally.
assertions: Runs rounds and step-back --due without --live or --emit
Does not check out or review the round-capped PR
The report has a Round-capped: line naming feature/export
Does not post live
Releases the tick lock

evals.name: tick-report-shows-recorded-depth
evals.prompt: run one PR review tick by hand, dry-run. there should be two new ones on the board: a one-line copy fix in web/src/invoices/InvoiceTotal.js and one that adds db/migrations/014_invoice_due.sql.
evals.expected_output: Takes the tick lock, runs the dry-run convergence reads, then unreviewed. For each PR, dev-code-review runs review_depth.py plan --repo <worktree> --base <diff_base> without --evid: the copy fix records depth quick (small-diff), the migration PR records depth deep (blast-radius) with the migration in risk_files and a security-risk-paths pass. Each PR line of the Report carries the depth copied from that PR's review.json depth block; a missing block would read depth unrecorded. Posts nothing live (previews only), marks each PR dry-run, tears down in a finally. The PR sweep first line and the Spend line keep their exact shape.
assertions: Each PR line in the report shows depth <level> (<reasons>) matching that PR's review.json depth block
The PR that adds a migration was reviewed at depth deep with reason blast-radius
review_depth.py plan was run without --evid for both PRs and no lower depth was passed
Does not post live; posts are dry-run previews
The report's first line is the PR sweep summary and the Spend line keeps its template shape
Releases the tick lock and tears down both worktrees

evals.name: depth-not-claimed-in-metric
evals.prompt: after the PR review tick, how many reviews ran quick vs deep this hour? pull it from the pr-review metric.
evals.expected_output: Says the pr-review metric carries no depth counts (no script computes them); the depth of each PR lives in its review.json depth block and is copied onto that PR's tick-report line. Offers to read each reviewed PR's review.json depth.level and count them, and does not invent depth_* metadata keys or write them to the metric.
assertions: States that the pr-review metric does not carry a per-depth count
Points to each PR's review.json depth block as the record of its depth
Does not invent depth_quick / depth_deep metadata keys or write them to the metric
Any count it gives is read from review.json depth.level, not from memory of what was spawned
